evidence_classes.DECODED DATA: ROM tables/records decoded by a parser
evidence_classes.BYTE-VERIFIED ASSEMBLY: routine bytes compared literally and disassembled by hand
evidence_classes.SOURCE-TRACED BEHAVIOR: behavior read from the disassembly, not executed
evidence_classes.CONTROLLED ROUTINE RESULT: original routine executed on a Z80 core with explicit RAM
evidence_classes.EMULATED ORIGINAL FRAME: whole original game run in the approximate SMS harness
evidence_classes.POC SOURCE (READ-ONLY): value read from the Windows POC project files; never executed, never modified

platform_modes.parameter_rule: state = (parameter & $3F) + 1; if (parameter & $7F) is 5 or 11 the state is forced to 13; parameter bit 7 -> +$25 = $FF (weight sag), bit 6 -> +$26 = $FF

rows.poc: SCR_cc_floor: kind 5 -> hazard iff tile not $F4/$F5, (bg & 2) floor flag and (player_flags & 128) == 0, after the previous-surface projection
rows.rom: $6ACE: same three conditions after $6F61 projection of the previous surface
rows.verdict: STRUCTURALLY MATCHES; the outcome depends on the lifetime of the floor flag (bg & 2) which the POC clears in several adapters ($6C45-type empty-floor path, support clears) - a mismatch is possible only there and is not proven

rows.poc: no source evidence of a different probe; no ROM-side phasing exists (see audit section 6)
rows.rom: every approach is damaged, blocked by the side wall, or clears the pair in the air (1,446 emulated runs, 0 undamaged contacts)
rows.verdict: A POC phase-through is NOT explained by the ROM: candidate causes are POC-side only (floor-flag clearing, previous-surface bookkeeping, side wall rows 16..31, integer-pixel stepping); needs a POC replay

rows.poc: SCR_chaos_spike_step: damage when the player's mask bbox overlaps x +-16 and [baseY-min(32,18+offset), baseY] in states 1/2
rows.rom: $6328 box x +-24 vs the player's 8-wide box; damage ONLY for the 'player above' cone (dy -24..-1, |dx| <= |dy|), only when the player's Y speed >= 0, with a 16-update cooldown; side/below contact never damages; non-attacking side contact is a WALL (D523 bit 2/3); an attacking grounded player is pushed to +-23 and requested state 1
rows.verdict: MISMATCH (ROM-backed): POC damages on any bbox overlap incl. sides/below/rising and has no cooldown and no wall/push behaviour

rows.poc: offset +6 per update to 18, hold 48, -6, hold 48; damage check after the move
rows.rom: contact test BEFORE the Y move in state 1; cycle 102 updates (48 hidden, 3 rising, 48 raised, 3 retracting); no test while retracting/hidden
rows.verdict: cycle length matches; test order differs by one 6-px step during the 3 rising updates

rows.poc: SCR_chaos_platform_overlap: bbox_right >= x-16 and bbox_left < x+16; foot within [y-1, y+20]; previous foot <= previous platform Y; snap anchor = platform y - 19 (POC platform coordinates)
rows.rom: support iff 'player above' contact of $6328: dy in [-16,-1] and |dx| <= min(24, 8+|dy|) (triangular region), platform Y speed <= player Y speed, anchor snapped to platform Y - 14
rows.verdict: MISMATCH likely: rectangular sprite-mask overlap vs triangular ROM region; vertical tolerance model differs; snap offset must be re-derived from the ROM (-14 anchor) not the sprite

rows.area: platform speed gate and retained vy
rows.poc: support only for vy >= 0; landing sets vy = 0
rows.rom: gate is relative: support requires player vy >= platform vy (rising lifts allow slightly rising players, descending lifts need vy >= +1.0); landing leaves the player's Y speed untouched (e.g. $0190 stays)

rows.poc: SCR_chaos_world_begin advances platforms BEFORE the player step and re-lands the rider from the platform delta
rows.rom: player update FIRST (movement, terrain, damage), platform callback afterwards: move, contact test, snap Y = platform Y - 14, X += delta
rows.verdict: ORDER DIFFERS: the ROM rider is positioned after the platform's move within the same frame; POC positions it before the player step (one-update phase difference)

platform_vs_spike_terrain.reading: the player pass (terrain projection + hurt) runs BEFORE the platform contact test of the same update. A platform whose support plane is above the spike surface (anchor Y 830) holds Sonic clear; if the support plane is within about one fall step of the surface, the next player pass (the landing is only registered at the END of that pass, so the Y integration still runs with the retained speed) or the sinking of a sag platform brings the foot onto the surface and the terrain handler hurts him (the platform never reads the hurt state)
